messages.author: 72848d54e6872c86
messages.subject: categorical variables in R
parts:
Dear all, 

I'm facing an issue when using the INLA models with mesh for spatial analyses: if I fit a categorical variable with more than 2 values, when I call the summary of the model I find two "anomalies":

1) I have a coefficient estimate for every value, while I'd expect one of them to be the reference, so I don't understand exactly how to interprete them
2) the standard errors are 30 to 40 times bigger than the value of the beta

I guessed I was doing something wrong, but reading the books about INLA I found the same result in all the examples that include such variables. 

If I build dichotomous variables for every contrast it seems like I can solve the issue, but I'd prefer to use the usual formulas. Does anybody know how to fix it? 

Thanks!!!

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] categorical variables in R
parts:
Hi,

You could, manually, turn the factor into several 0-1 numeric covariates, and compare to your result. I prefer to do this conversion myself, instead of letting INLA handle it, so that I am in complete control of what is going on.

It is typical to see posterior standard deviation of 31. This happens if there are no data with a certain level of the categorical variable.

In some cases, I strongly suggest using an IID effect instead of a "fixed effect".

Kind regards,
Haakon
